content_sections.body: Start with the model: 'What time did the coach leave, and why was it late?' Replace one detail with your own information about asking about a late coach. Then add a short follow-up or reason. This builds the skill to ask and answer short questions about a journey or delay.
content_sections.title: Build a useful turn (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about asking about a late coach. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Ask and answer short questions about a journey or delay.
content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)

content_sections.body: Create a short message about asking about a late coach without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.
content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)

listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about asking about a late coach.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.

pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in asking about a late coach easy to hear.
pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for asking about a late coach in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in travel questions and answers

constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about asking about a late coach.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay asking about a late coach. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about asking about a late coach.
writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about asking about a late coach. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
